task.description:
FINAL RE-GATE of the ISS-0426 design (rework 2, commit 740368dd). You have already PASSED everything except check 1(c), across two prior gate passes: 1(a), 1(b), the reconciled counts, the mixed-tests decision, the scope header and AC4 are all settled and MUST NOT be re-litigated. This re-gate has exactly ONE question, plus a scope-discipline confirmation.

THE ONE QUESTION -- does check 1(c) now clear? Your required fix was: state an explicit, binding usage contract on section 2.1.2's seam rather than leaving its safety as an observation about current usage. CODE-DESIGNER added section 2.1.2a ('Binding usage contract on this seam') and, for the sibling defect ORCH folded in, section 2.1.1b plus a two-row comparison table classifying section 2.1.1's seam as CATEGORICAL (mechanism-enforced) and section 2.1.2's as CONTRACTUAL (caller discipline). Judge whether the contract as written actually binds:
  (a) Is it stated as a RULE a future caller must obey, not as a description of what today's callers happen to do?
  (b) Does it state the failure mode concretely enough that someone who violates it will recognise what they broke?
  (c) Is the contract text specified as something that lands in the seam's OWN @doc false -- so a future caller reading only the source, never this design doc, gets the rule? This was the substance of the finding: a design-doc-only contract does not bind a caller who never reads the design doc.
  (d) Is the categorical-vs-contractual distinction in section 2.1.1b accurate? Specifically check the claim that Lua source can escape the OUTCOME of the :max_instructions counter (by pcall-catching the raised error) but cannot escape the counter INCREMENTING, and the stated `goto` caveat. If that claim is wrong the table misclassifies section 2.1.1's seam as safer than it is, which would be a worse defect than the one you FAILED on -- so verify it rather than accepting it.

SCOPE-DISCIPLINE CONFIRMATION. The rework was instructed to change nothing else. CODE-DESIGNER reports it also made two small consistency touches adjacent to the fix (tightening section 2.1.2's 'not a live risk' bullet to point forward to the new contract, and adding one checklist item to section 4 so a validator can confirm the contract's presence as a one-time source read). Confirm via git diff (740368dd against its parent) that the revision is confined to the contract fix plus those two touches and the status line -- and that no seam mechanism, count, table row, tag-wiring detail, or the letflow.check.test.ex change moved. A rework that silently altered a gate-approved element is itself a FAIL.

BIAS TOWARD CLOSING. This is rework 2 of max 3; a FAIL here leaves one attempt before ORCH must escalate per ORCHESTRATOR.md. The remaining defect class is documentation wording, not mechanism. If the contract binds and the distinction is accurate, PASS it -- do not hold the gate for stylistic preferences or for wording you would have phrased differently. If it genuinely does not bind, FAIL with the exact sentence(s) required, so rework 3 is a mechanical edit rather than another interpretation cycle.

On PASS set next_action to route to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation. Do not edit lib/ or test/. Commit your handoff to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.

result.summary:
FINAL RE-GATE: PASS. Scope per the coordinator's instruction: only check 1(c) (the deadlock-risk contract gap) was open; 1(a), 1(b), the reconciled counts, the mixed-tests decision, the scope header, and AC4 were already settled across the prior two gates and are not re-litigated here.

SCOPE-DISCIPLINE CONFIRMATION (checked first, via git diff 740368dd^ 740368dd, not accepted from the rework report): the entire diff is 147 inserted / 15 removed lines in lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md plus its own handoff record -- zero other files touched. Every REMOVED line in the design doc diff (grepped explicitly) is exactly: the status line, and the '605/644's workloads are the same bounded... not a live risk' bullet CODE-DESIGNER reported tightening -- nothing else. Confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD --stat` that executor.ex, test_helper.exs, and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex remain completely absent from this branch's diff (zero code written, as expected for a design-only step) -- no seam mechanism, table row, count, or tag-wiring detail moved anywhere in this rework.

CHECK 1(c) -- THE ONE QUESTION:

(a) Rule, not usage description -- YES. The new section 2.1.2a's blockquote reads 'Callers of this seam MUST pass a workload that is guaranteed to terminate on its own, independently of any wall-clock enforcement' -- modal, imperative, addressed to future callers, closing with an explicit routing consequence ('it belongs in Group 2 ... never in this seam'). This is a rule with a consequence, not a description of what today's two callers happen to do.

(b) Failure mode concrete enough to recognize -- YES. 'A script that can catch its own instruction-budget exhaustion (e.g. via pcall) and continue executing is NOT a valid input to this seam: nothing will terminate it, and the calling test process will hang until ExUnit's own test timeout, not the seam's.' Names the exact violating shape (pcall-trap-and-continue), the exact consequence (unbounded hang), and the exact backstop (ExUnit's default 60s) -- a violator who hits this and sees a 60s ExUnit timeout has enough here to trace it back to the rule they broke.

(c) Lands in the seam's own @doc false, not only the design doc -- YES, explicitly instructed, not merely implied: 'this is the binding text -- ELIXIR-DEV must carry this into the seam's own @doc false declaration, not merely into a design doc nobody reads at the call site.' Section 7's OQ-1 note (present from rework 1, unchanged by this rework per the diff) reinforces this: 'Latitude here is naming/arity only -- it does not extend to section 2.1.2a's binding usage contract text ... which is not latitude and must appear in that seam's own @doc false content verbatim in substance.' This closes the exact gap the prior FAIL named: a design-doc-only contract does not bind a caller who never reads the design doc; this one is explicitly instructed to travel into the source.

(d) Section 2.1.1b's categorical-vs-contractual distinction -- VERIFIED ACCURATE against the actual dependency source, not accepted from the design's moduledoc quotes alone. Read deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/state.ex's tick!/2 (the instruction-budget charge/raise function) and deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/dispatcher.ex's call sites of tick/4 directly. Two independent findings:
  - The pcall-catches-outcome-not-increment claim is TRUE. tick!/2 raises a catchable Lua.VM.RuntimeError once the tally reaches max_instructions -- pcall can catch that raise (the outcome), but the tally itself is threaded as a plain function argument through dispatch/12's recursion, entirely in the Elixir interpreter, with no Lua-level hook or intercept point on the increment itself. Confirmed by reading every tick(...) call site in dispatcher.ex: they occur at while/repeat/numeric_for/generic_for loop back-edges (state.ex's own tick!/2 docstring: 'Call it at loop back-edges and call boundaries -- never per opcode') and at call-opcode dispatch. A pcall around the raised error stops the error from propagating; it cannot roll back or suppress the tally that already fired.
  - The goto caveat is TRUE and precisely where the design says it is. Read dispatcher.ex:1715-1721 (@op_goto's two clauses) directly: both call dispatch/12 with instruction_count threaded UNCHANGED -- goto never calls tick. This structurally confirms REQ-155 AC-2's own workload (executor_test.exs:389-396, pcall-catch-then-goto-loop) is a genuine, real escape from the instruction counter, exactly as the design states, and exactly why layer 2/the wall-clock kill exists at all.
  - ONE IMPRECISION FOUND, ASSESSED AS NON-BLOCKING: section 2.1.1b's prose says max_instructions is 'enforced by the Lua VM interpreter itself on every opcode it executes' -- the actual mechanism charges at loop back-edges and call boundaries only (confirmed by state.ex's own docstring and by tracing every tick call site), not literally every opcode. This does NOT misclassify section 2.1.1's seam as safer than it is: straight-line bytecode between two ticked boundaries is a fixed, already-compiled sequence with no way to run unboundedly without itself looping or calling, both of which tick -- so the categorical-bound CONCLUSION (bounded for any input except a goto-based escape) is still correct under the true, finer-grained mechanism. The two-row table's actual claims (CATEGORICAL for 2.1.1, CONTRACTUAL for 2.1.2, with the goto caveat named) are accurate. This is a wording imprecision in the supporting rationale, not a defect in the classification -- flagged as a non-blocking should-fix, not grounds for FAIL, per the coordinator's own framing that a wrong claim (not an imprecise gloss on a claim that remains true) would be the disqualifying case.

OVERALL: PASS. Check 1(c) clears on all three sub-criteria plus the accuracy verification -- 1(a), 1(b), 2, 3 remain settled and unrelitigated from prior gates. The remaining defect class really is documentation wording (the 'every opcode' imprecision), not mechanism, matching the coordinator's own read; holding the gate for it would be exactly the over-insistence the coordinator warned against. This design (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md, commit 740368dd) is unambiguous enough to build from: both seams' behavior, contracts, and coverage consequences are fully specified, no implementation code is present, every ISS-0426 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element (section 5), and the two open questions remaining (OQ-1/renamed-OQ-3 naming latitude, OQ-4/renamed-OQ-3 tag-conflict grep) are genuine implementation latitude, not unresolved design questions.

issues.description: Section 2.1.1b describes max_instructions as enforced 'on every opcode it executes' -- independently verified against deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/state.ex's tick!/2 docstring and every tick/4 call site in deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/dispatcher.ex that the actual charging granularity is loop back-edges and call boundaries, not literally every opcode. Does not change the categorical-bound conclusion (still true: any straight-line run between two ticked boundaries is a fixed, finite, already-compiled instruction sequence) or misclassify the seam, so not gate-blocking -- worth a one-word tightening ('at each loop iteration and call' in place of 'on every opcode') the next time this section is touched for any other reason, not worth its own rework cycle.

result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a) for implementation. The design (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md, commit 740368dd) is APPROVED: both new @doc false test-only seams (section 2.1.1a candidate (i) for the nil-heap path, section 2.1.2 plus 2.1.2a's binding usage contract for the heap-limited path) are fully specified, the heap-limited seam's contract text must be carried verbatim in substance into its own @doc false declaration per section 2.1.2a and section 7's OQ-1 note -- this is a build requirement, not latitude. ELIXIR-DEV should also apply the one MINOR wording note above opportunistically if touching section 2.1.1b's prose for any other reason, but it is not a blocking requirement.
